principle: Each project has one primary role and many orthogonal traits. Product role and storage/retrieval architecture must never be conflated.

primary_roles.name: Human-first PKM / workspace
primary_roles.definition: A user-facing system whose canonical workflow is human writing, organizing, linking, and revisiting knowledge.

primary_roles.name: AI knowledge app / RAG brain
primary_roles.definition: A user-facing assistant that ingests documents or connected sources and answers, searches, summarizes, or automates over them.

primary_roles.name: External agent-memory service
primary_roles.definition: A library or service outside the agent runtime that extracts, stores, retrieves, and manages durable memories through an SDK, API, or tool protocol. The agent can be replaced while the memory remains.

primary_roles.name: Temporal context / knowledge-graph engine
primary_roles.definition: Infrastructure that represents entities, relationships, provenance, and often changing truth over time rather than only flat chunks.

primary_roles.name: Stateful agent runtime / harness
primary_roles.definition: The agent itself owns identity, durable state, skills, schedules, and a memory lifecycle as part of its runtime.

primary_roles.name: Coding-agent workflow / skill stack
primary_roles.definition: Prompts, roles, tools, and process that turn a coding agent into a repeatable software-delivery system. Memory may be present, but software execution is primary.

primary_roles.name: Human–agent memory bridge
primary_roles.definition: A compatibility layer that exposes human-owned files or workspaces to multiple agents, usually through MCP, skills, CLI, or an API.

primary_roles.name: Ambient capture / lifelogging
primary_roles.definition: A passive collector that records digital activity such as active apps, screen snapshots, audio, or events without requiring deliberate note creation.

primary_roles.name: Retrieval / storage infrastructure
primary_roles.definition: A low-level vector, graph, lexical, or multimodal store used to build memory systems; not a second brain by itself.

primary_roles.name: Research / benchmark / reference
primary_roles.definition: A survey, benchmark, course, template, or catalog that informs implementation but is not itself a complete operational second brain.

architectures.name: Vector / embedding index
architectures.note: An architecture trait, not a product category.

license_scopes.name: Open-source core plus restricted enterprise code
Source visible but commercially or otherwise restricted

score_dimensions.definition: How directly useful the project is as a personal or agentic second brain.
Local-first behavior, exportability, privacy, and user control.
Open formats, APIs, adapters, and model/provider portability.
Retrieval, temporal handling, provenance, consolidation, and contradiction management.
Setup and maintenance burden for a technically capable individual.
Adoption, maintenance, documentation, and production readiness.
